analysis:
The changed files are offline release-pipeline tests (scripts/test-provider-release-resolution.py, scripts/test-provider-release-resume.py, scripts/test-release-dev-branch.py). They contain no runtime provider, coordinator, cache or attestation code. The tests pin new release-routing semantics: a master push publishes staging only, and a dev push publishes dev only with a -dev.branch.N version. A dispatched dev run resolves only as an unpublished validation build. Prod and staging from a dev push, and dev or prod from a master push, fail closed with no outputs. Resolution still rejects non-dev, non-master branch pushes, devx and dev/x refs, bad run numbers, newline injection and version overrides on pushes. Test-side changes are mostly stricter: a dev push is verified as GitHub-signed, on dev ancestry and for environment dev only. The resume test pins that dev ancestry never substitutes for master ancestry on master routes. Prod resume stays restricted to current reviewed master dispatch.

Relevant threat IDs: T-054 (build identity provenance, A-017) and T-013 (binary integrity) concern the release trust path. The changed tests do not weaken them, but they only assert behavior. I could not see resolve-provider-release.sh, provider_release_resume/api.py, release-provider.yml or release-dev-branch.yml, so whether the production code enforces these tests (especially dev-branch ancestry via git/ref/heads/dev, and the prod signing-identity isolation) is unverified. The test-release-dev-branch.py body is not visible, only its metadata and a patch excerpt. The next pass should check that the dev lane cannot reach prod secrets or the production Apple signing identity. It should also check that dev-branch push protections match the master gate, because dev pushes now publish signed builds to the DEV coordinator with secrets: inherit. No concrete regression is visible in the supplied evidence.
